message.content: In late fifteenth and early sixteenth century Poland, Copernicus worked amid a complex political landscape where the Lithuanian union, royal centralization, and local magnate power shaped institutions. The Renaissance brought renewed interest in classical learning, while the Church retained doctrinal authority and universities guarded Aristotelian cosmology. Patronage from canon law courts and the church allowed him to develop astronomical calculations without overtly challenging scriptural interpretation. His model, though not cactiform in appearance, used a heliocentric arrangement to simplify planetary motion and reduce epicyclic complications.
